bundestag.summary:
SUMMARY:
The 75th session of the 21st legislative period of the German Bundestag took place on Friday, April 24, 2026. The session featured a comprehensive agenda focused on economic and tax-related legislation, as well as transport policy. A significant portion of the day was dedicated to the second and third readings of several key legislative proposals. These included a draft law by the CDU/CSU and SPD factions to temporarily reduce energy tax on fuels, known as the Second Energy Tax Reduction Act. Additionally, BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN introduced a bill to amend the Electricity Tax Act and other regulations. The Finance Committee presented recommendations and reports concerning various motions, including proposals from the AfD to immediately relieve working commuters by increasing the mileage allowance and to refrain from introducing a windfall tax while addressing high fuel prices. Die Linke also put forward a motion to effectively relieve the population and economy from rising fuel prices. This was linked to a motion by BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN to view the price shock from fossil fuels as a wake-up call and accelerate independence from coal, oil, and gas. Further discussions involved the second and third readings of a governmental draft to amend the Tax Consultancy Act, alongside reports from the Budget Committee and Finance Committee on motions related to modernizing the tax consultancy profession and strengthening municipal tax revenue. The agenda also included a motion by Die Linke to relieve private households with a nine-euro ticket and a recommendation from the Transport Committee on a motion by BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN to revise the Municipal Transport Financing Act and secure the expansion of public transport. Numerous MPs from various factions contributed to the debates, with specific page numbers indicating when their contributions can be found in the full transcript.

No discussion about Ukrainian men found in this session.

facts.fact: During the Edo period in Japan, sumptuary laws dictated the colors and fabrics that different social classes could wear. For example, only the imperial family and high-ranking samurai could wear bright red, while commoners were restricted to more muted earth tones and simple cottons. These regulations were a powerful tool for maintaining social hierarchy and preventing the merchant class from appearing too opulent.

The ancient Greek festival of the Anthesteria involved a ritualistic drinking contest where the winner received a garland of flowers and a year's supply of wine.  This festival was dedicated to Dionysus, the god of wine, fertility, and revelry, and included ceremonies like the opening of wine jars and a procession of Dionysus's sacred boat. It was one of the oldest and most significant festivals in Athens.
